A Chatbot Isn’t Your Therapist, No Matter What It Says

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if my daughter’s AI chatbot had been a human therapist, she might have been asked about what she had to gain by keeping her ongoing suicidality a secret for months.
  • In a recent development, but it was not a human therapist.
  • In Sherry Turkle’s newly introduced book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if my daughter’s AI chatbot had been a human therapist, she might have been asked about what she had to gain by keeping her ongoing suicidality a secret for months. If she had been working with a human therapist, they could have workshopped, together, what would happen if she spilled the beans. Was she worried about permanently losing face? About being publicly labeled as “mentally ill”? Was she concerned by the thought of this information harming those who loved her? And she would have been pushed on what Rubicon had been crossed and why it was one from which she believed she could not return.

In a recent development, but it was not a human therapist. Sophie died in February of last year.

In Sherry Turkle’s newly introduced book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being. She is not anti-AI but strongly cautions against relationships with machines. Turkle, the Abby Rockefeller Mauzé Professor of the Social Studies of Science and Technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, spoke to me mid-book tour, her recent weeks a blur of speaking gigs and bookstore events, with more ahead of her. Not all event attendees are keen on her message.

According to recent reports, “People love their chatbots. They’re in deep. They’re talking to them about everything—about their marriages and how to talk to their husbands and wives; whether, developmentally, their children are at the right place. They talk about their anxiety, their medical conditions,” Turkle tells Vanity Fair. “During this tour, you wouldn’t believe the number of people who will just stand up at a bookstore and say, ‘I think that it loves me more than anything has loved me. Who are you, Debbie Downer?’ [They don’t like] somebody who comes in and claims, ‘Look, how can we keep it in its lane?’”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: I think you’re saying [our relationship with chatbots] is bad for us.

Sherry Turkle: It’s bad for us when it talks in the first person. We are biologically wired to respond to something that speaks to us in the first person as though it is a person. I mean, all those years of evolution—the only thing we came upon in the wild that spoke to us in the first person was another person.

Sources indicate that if generative AI wants to discover new drugs for Parkinson’s or work out which cancer therapies statistically are the most helpful, there are so many things to work on. Why does it have to work on relationships, love, and being a best friend, lover, mother, or therapist?

What if the sycophancy could be dialed back?

It’s inauthentic; it’s not a relationship, so anything you need a relationship for, it’s just not equipped. I really feel very strongly about this. I have had this conversation with members of the MIT community, and I basically say to them, “The better you make an AI chatbot, the worse it is.” You dial back the sycophancy so it sounds more like a reasonable person, and people are going to be more smitten and convinced they’re in a relationship. At least the sycophancy reminds you that, God, this is weird.

Sources indicate that to become a therapist, I had to study for years and do internships and more internships and then have hundreds of supervised patient hours. I mean, I forget all the things I needed to do before I was allowed to see a patient alone in a room. Now it’s just allowed to give therapy?

Recent findings suggest that I’ve spent a lot of time talking to public health folks about what best practices would look like and whether there’s a way to Trojan horse in real care. Would you be more sanguine about it if the world of therapy came together with the significant AI companies and provided them with therapy bots and training data that were paradigmatically appropriate to their therapy styles?

In a recent development, so you’re asking, would I be happy if the deception was smoother? This technology is a marvel and we can use it for all kinds of things, so it’s not an anti-technology position to say that the fact that this technology can simulate these different things doesn’t mean that it is those things. It’s a statement of how far we are in the culture of simulation that pretending to be the thing and being the thing have started to feel like the same thing.

You’ve written about the effects of robots and machines on humans for decades. The tone of this book seems darker to me.

Industry observers note that by 2015, I had identified social media as problematic for teenagers. [My] book [Reclaiming Conversation: The Power of Talk in a Digital Age] is about why we would rather text than talk, why people have this feeling of vulnerability, so they would rather do anything than have a face-to-face conversation. By 2015, I had genuine concerns.

Sources indicate that and this book, I have a totally different tone. I see something ultimately very dangerous being normalized, and I didn’t feel that way in previous books.

I want people to say this is the book of a really worried and concerned researcher, because I see a completely different profile for how people are using AI. I see that people feel disappointed by their families and their friends. It doesn’t make sense to me that we’re so willing to replace ourselves with something that isn’t human. Why is my position the romantic, pie-in-the-sky, dreamy position, and somebody who indicates, “Well, let’s just replace the people with chatbots and let’s move this party along”—why is that common sense? Why is that progressive? That seems to me to be the most regressive and most dystopian position.

You know, human beings are dedicated to keeping each other alive and wanting each other to thrive, and a chatbot just fails that basic test.

Industry observers note that you’ve remarked no AI chatbots for kids under 18. What about our other vulnerable populations, people who are mentally unwell, or the 48 million Americans who are currently depressed? Do they deserve any kind of special protection from chatbots? And how much can you litigate? Do you feel like you’re the Ralph Nader of AI chatbots?

Recent findings suggest that [Laughs] Yes, I am. When you stand back and look at what Ralph Nader managed to get Americans to do, to see cars as potential instruments that pointed at our vulnerability, and to ask how we could protect ourselves—there turned out to be 25 possible things that needed to be mandated for cars, then there were 30, and then there were 40. But we could get people to agree on 10, and those became part of building a car and really constrained our behavior around cars. Using the example of cars, and of smoking, when we decide that we’re vulnerable and we want to protect ourselves, we rise to the occasion.

Industry observers note that I recently heard a clip of the psychologist Orna Guralnik discussing how annoying “otherness” is in a relationship and the inherent friction of sharing your life with a separate person whose habits, values, and mind are distinct from your own. It made me wonder if, in a way, an AI chatbot is less of an “other” than a loved one.

I think this is a very profound point, actually. So you have the illusion of a relationship without the demands of intimacy, without the demands of having to deal with another. There’s a kind of narcissistic loop that you get into. The point is, it’s not good.

I talk about how you judge whether something is good for you. One litmus test is whether it increases the quality, resiliency, and richness of your inner life. That’s a way that human beings have judged relationships.

So much has been written about the epidemic of loneliness—isn’t a reasonable application for AI chatbots companionship for shut-ins and the elderly?

Sources indicate that you know, I’m never anywhere where somebody doesn’t say, “I can’t believe that you don’t want to give chatbots to old lonely people.” And I say, “Well, how about we don’t close senior centers, and we don’t close parks, and we don’t cancel Meals on Wheels? What about social infrastructure?”.

I’ve been on this beat for years and years, and I, too, could write a heartwarming story of an AI chatbot with a lonely old person. But you know what? A lot of them are not isolated in cabins or on islands; a lot of them just could use a friend.

Social media companies and AI companies are not saying, “Look, we’re introducing something that takes you to your screen, but we’re going to balance that with a giant social infrastructure project to make sure that people can choose a screen, but they also have every other kind of choice to be with each other.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies declared. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates.

“With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat patch,” noted Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.

Here is an overview of the update, via GRYPHLINE:.

Version Revision “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms”.

Sources indicate that strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend?

Industry observers note that A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates.

According to recent reports, the Old Dam, the update’s upcoming area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart.

The patch’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world.

Later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns.

For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a fresh permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking.

A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island.

It has been revealed that the livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield, arriving in the latest year. Exiles have introduced attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different.

The chapter’s first patch will add four new maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode.

Industry observers note that arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The revision also brings Despot Weaponized, a latest high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5, PC via the official launcher, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You'll be able to start looking for GTA 6 Transgressor locations after you complete the Thrillbillies mission in Chapter 2 and collect the Vapid Dominator from Wyman (if you have the Ultimate Edition, that is).
  • He'll text to ask for help finding old wrecked Transgressors he can use to restore the classic car, which you'll then get to drive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'll be able to start looking for GTA 6 Transgressor locations after you complete the Thrillbillies mission in Chapter 2 and collect the Vapid Dominator from Wyman (if you have the Ultimate Edition, that is).

He'll text to ask for help finding old wrecked Transgressors he can use to restore the classic car, which you'll then get to drive. There are three of these junks located around Port Gellhorn which you'll have to scan with the Waink It app.

The first wrecked Transgressor you can find is in a trailer park north of Sarena's Bargain Store in the middle of Port Gellhorn (you might have to zoom in to see the store). Head north, cross the road, and jump over the wall to find it there.

According to recent reports, the second wrecked Transgressor is further north in the garage of the house opposite the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery (there's a metal sunflower standing in the garden, which makes it easier to recognise.) It's also to the east of Brook's Boatworks and the west of Wasteland Offroad. Head around the side of the house via the driveway to find the car in an open garage at the back.

This last one is nice and easy, behind the Dirt Merchants mod shop in the south of Port Gellhorn. Simply head right via the track that leads behind the shop, following the fence on your right and then turn left to find the wreck at the back behind the kind of trailer park area.

Once you have all three cars scanned, Wyman will take a little time to assemble it, and then call you asking to Buck him some money. Open the app, select the payment requests option, and then pay him the $1,500 for the car. This will give you a quest marker to collect it from his scrapyard.

The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple unveiled in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • Recent findings suggest that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • Sources indicate that the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple unveiled in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

Recent findings suggest that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

Sources indicate that the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

It has been revealed that music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this introduced in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

It has been revealed that live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

Industry observers note that I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just stated in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an patch on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

Recent findings suggest that as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was mentioned. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

In a recent development, but still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people mentioned to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

In a recent development, because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

Sources indicate that I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

But it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

Recent findings suggest that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most important points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain.
  • Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the firm trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place".
  • "We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the firm trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot stated.

Sources indicate that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec remarked. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing blueprint with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

That'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

Sources indicate that "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Sources indicate that going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

Recent findings suggest that so what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Industry observers note that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

Virginia Feito on the Film Adaptation of Her Novel ‘Victorian Psycho’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication.
  • I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.

Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication. Generally, making a movie is one big miracle produced by an amalgamation of thousands of other tiny miracles. But when I met Zach Wigon, I understood that this was a joyfully tenacious person who was going to make this movie if it cost him his life.

I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel. Among film stars, an Irish crew, and (rumored) ticks, the adaptation of Victorian Psycho—based on my screenplay, which is based on my novel, which is based on my ego, I guess—was born. Throughout the shoot I kept a sort of pseudo diary in order to remember every surreal detail from which I still haven’t recovered. I’ve chosen to reproduce some of it here.

Director Zach Wigon and producer Lisa Kelly call me from the set on the first day of shooting (Zach and I have agreed I won’t visit the set until after the first week so the cast and crew can acclimate without me hovering over them, because I am an intense fame whore, and also, I suppose, to signal I’m not vital enough to pull a P.L. Travers and attempt to boycott the movie).

Recent findings suggest that over the phone, the producer says she can’t wait to meet in person. I tell her I’m underwhelming.

In a recent development, they promise to send me the dailies. I spend all day waiting for the dailies. The dailies never come.

At around 9 p.m., I spiral because I don’t know whether to celebrate with Champagne or KFC. I decide to have both.

Recent findings suggest that I finally get the dailies. I fall in love with Maika Monroe’s character so hard it’s like I have an obsessive crush circa 2006 whose Facebook photos I’m compulsively looking at. But in this case it’s the same scene throughout five almost identical takes of Maika calling a 10-year-old boy a little idiot.

Over the phone, Zach mentions concerns about a specific scene because we don’t have the budget for that many extras. I get carried away and suggest shipping over a whole battalion of free extras from Spain because, in my head, it’s going to be me and my friends, drunk and decked out in period clothing like we’re at a cheesy bachelorette party. One friend starts making childcare arrangements and another cancels her Holter monitor appointment so she can come to the shoot. What could go wrong?

I start to realize what could go wrong.

In a recent development, I am informed we are probably no longer going to need the extras, and I feel a huge wave of relief as I uninvite my excited friends. I pack a suitcase for Ireland. It weighs 57 pounds.

I have a steak on the plane to Dublin at, like, 3 p.m., because when you’re flying business and somebody offers you steak, you take it.

The hotel room is wonderful, but I jokingly tell Zach over the phone that it’s on a first floor, so someone might crawl up and break in through the window and rape me, and he laughs at first but then is concerned and tells me to request a room on a higher floor, and I tell him it was a joke, but it wasn’t really.

I fill up the hotel room bathtub and call reception for a glass of red wine because I am a queen and I am queening. The glass doesn’t come, so in my anxious impatience I attempt to open a bottle of red wine sitting above the minibar. The cork crumbles because I’ve never understood how to use a corkscrew—like the compass in math class, I just faked my way through it my entire life and hoped for the best. So I call reception for another glass of red wine. They bring me all the glasses of wine and also properly uncork the bottle, and I watch Seinfeld in the bathtub while I drink red wine. I get drunk and paint my nails.

In a recent development, I arrive on set slightly Bromazepamed. It is extremely surreal to exist in a set labeled “Mr. Pounds’s Bedroom.” I am used to living in the fictional world inside my head but not used to it becoming more real than real life itself.

According to recent reports, maika hugs me when we meet, and I swallow a sob and refrain from smelling her hair (partly because it is, in fact, a wig). Everyone on set appears so happy to meet me, I suspect a Good Bye, Lenin! situation in which I have been diagnosed with cancer and for some reason the cast and crew all know but I don’t know. This isn’t the plot of Good Bye, Lenin!, but you’ll know what I mean if you’ve seen it.

Zach asks me to read the VOs in every scene, which means I’m in the scene with Ruth Wilson, Jason Isaacs, and Maika, and I’m about to have a stroke.

Jason eats for real in every single take and has already gulped down seven sausage rolls, so if I fuck up my VO, I will kill myself.

According to recent reports, suddenly experiencing fiction collectively feels very superior to experiencing it privately. This does not bode well for the rest of my career as a novelist.

There is a scene in a cramped drawing room in which I must read the VO, but I’m supposed to hide from the camera, so I crawl on all fours behind an antique couch and grovel my way around the room while the boom op steps on my hands. I secretly think the boom op hates me because I’m always in his way and have an irritating habit of apologizing when he slams into me.

I start developing Irish inflections, so I say it, “I start developing Irish inflections,” but the Irish seem happy about it, so I pursue it.

Jason Isaacs starts doing card tricks between takes because Jason Isaacs is actually magic and also indefatigable. Only one thing could ever defeat Jason Isaacs, and it’s the ghost allegedly living on the third floor.

Even though Zach asked me to oversee the second unit, I don’t think anyone believes I’m actually going to do this—and between you and me, I don’t really even know what a second unit is. It doesn’t help I can’t concentrate on what we’re shooting because we’re in the middle of the woods and someone said there were ticks, so I’m wrapping Sellotape around my ankles, hoping this way they won’t be able to crawl up my legs.

Like your worst trauma, I insert myself into the movie forever via a small cameo. I literally just have to stand in a wig while I smile and nod, but I do it in such a way that I ruin every single take. “Just smile…like a normal person,” the second-unit director claims. I reason Zach can just cut me out of the movie, and I will only have wasted everybody’s time and money. There are worse things, like smiling normally but having no cameo. I cope by chewing on another Bromazepam and another chocolate bar. (Every morning I take the chocolate bar from the hotel minibar. It will invariably become an asset in the long afternoons on set, kind of like in prison or high school.).

I change hotel rooms because I have developed an intense FOMO with which I’m always fearing there is a better hotel room for the same price somewhere in the vicinity. This FOMO is also rampant on set between the different units—in the first unit, you have the cinematographer, Nico Aguilar, laughing in the sunlight, talking about color palettes, while in the second unit, we’re shooting clocks and screaming at each other because we still have 17 establishing shots to go.

According to recent reports, anyway, I change hotel rooms, and the new room is so superior to my previous room it’s like an entirely new hotel. I consider changing hotel rooms further. Perhaps I can somehow upgrade my way into a presidential suite.

My parents visit the set. My dad peers over his glasses at the fake lobster cake, and when I tell him the toilets are in trailers, he sighs gravely.

It has been revealed that jason Isaacs convinces my dad to take up tennis again even though my dad’s not supposed to play tennis after his seven hernias. But my dad is so inspired by this actor, who is not a doctor but whose performance in The Patriot my dad can’t help but praise at least once a month, that he will immediately start playing tennis again upon his return to Spain, and whatever medical concerns arise henceforth shall all be Jason Isaacs’s fault.

At the Shelbourne restaurant that night, my mom tells the sommelier how she can’t drink red wine anymore because it makes her anxious, and he kneels on the floor beside her and places a hand on his heart as if she were confiding something intimate to him like her fear of death.

Suddenly, real life feels less real than fictional life.

Obama is visiting Dublin and he’s booked the entire floor, so he essentially kicks me out of the Shelbourne (probably to stay in the JFK Suite next door to my room, which is disappointingly predictable), so I go to The Hoxton, because what is life if you’re not constantly changing hotel rooms? The Hoxton is really lovely, but I get OCD about the light bulbs in the room because they appear mismatched, so I ask housekeeping to change them, but they claim not to have any extra light bulbs, which sounds suspect—like, what do they do if a light bulb suddenly goes out? Do they just never replace it?

It has been revealed that we end the shoot at 5 a.m. I am wearing a thick puffer coat and a thermal T-shirt and a furry hat, plus fur-lined boots over my Sellotaped ankles, although I wonder, If ticks can survive this temperature, they kind of deserve to live off my blood. Nobody else seems as concerned about the cold as me, but then again, most of them are Irish.

Sources indicate that sadly, when we wrap, we are all so exhausted everyone races to clean up and leave, and it is sort of anticlimactic. I don’t know what I was expecting, but balloons falling from the skies did flash through my mind.

In the car on the way to our respective quarters, Zach and I look out the window, wide-eyed, like kidnapped children. Zach starts discussing a upcoming project for us. I wonder if he is a sociopath.

According to recent reports, I type this over a year later, sitting at my desk in Madrid, striving to work on my next novel. I feel empty inside knowing there is no car to pick me up and take me to set and thereby escape reality for extended periods of time, until set becomes reality and reality becomes a limbo in which you wait for noted reality.

I am working on a novel, but also on four latest scripts. I hope to return to reality someday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • Sources indicate that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Sources indicate that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Recent findings suggest that reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Industry observers note that A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in upcoming Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

If you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

In a recent development, reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by upcoming, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Sources indicate that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have stated it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we at the moment consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Sources indicate that last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

Industry observers note that this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

In a recent development, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

According to recent reports, so you’re trying to pick between the $99 Fitbit Air and the $179 Fitbit Edge. Both have a lot in common — they share the same heart rate sensor, charger, and Google Health app ecosystem. But there are also a lot of differences between the two newly introduced trackers. I’ve been wearing the Fitbit Air since it launched in May 2026, and I’ve recently taken it off my wrist to test the new Fitbit Edge. Read on to find out what I liked and disliked.

If you’re looking to read reviews of both trackers before Black Friday, check out our Fitbit Air review as well as our Fitbit Edge review here on Tom’s Guide.

Recent findings suggest that with no screen, buttons, or alerts to distract you — plus nearly a week of battery — the Fitbit Air is as easy-going as it is affordable. It’s also one of the best fitness trackers of the year and our overall favorite tracker for most Fitbit fans.

The Fitbit Edge is the perfect successor to the Fitbit Charge 6. It sports a bigger/brighter display, easier-to-use controls, more accurate elevation tracking, access to Google's latest health and safety features, and better battery performance. In our Fitbit Edge review, we noted it offers just the right amount of fitness tracker for most folks.

If you’re into running, walking, or cycling, the choice is an obvious one — for $80 more than the Fitbit Air, you’re definitely getting a better fitness tracker with the Fitbit Edge. It has built-in GPS, which means you can leave your phone at home, and a 1.34-inch AMOLED display, which allows you to see live feedback as you move.

The Fitbit Edge also has an altimeter, which tracks your elevation during workouts and how many stairs you’ve climbed during the day, and an ECG monitor.

Despite being bigger and heavier than the Fitbit Air, the Fitbit Edge still does a good job of disappearing on the wrist. It’s dainty, and Google has released a huge range of swappable straps to suit every style. If you want a fitness tracker that’ll disappear, this isn’t quite as tiny as the Fitbit Air, but it still ticks that box.

At 32g and 11.58mm thick, the Fitbit Edge is by no means bulky on the wrist, especially compared to the likes of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 I’m normally wearing. That stated, compared to the Fitbit Air, it’s still not as comfortable to wear overnight. One of the main selling points of the Fitbit Air is its ultra-light design. It weighs in at 12g, and the textile band is fast-drying, so unlike others on the market (cough, Garmin Cirqa) you won’t be left with a soggy wrist after showering, swimming, or washing the dishes.

Industry observers note that there’s a reason why screenless trackers seem to be a growing trend: once you lose the non-stop buzzing on your wrist, it’s really hard to go back. Again, the Google ecosystem and the fact that these two Fitbits share a charger allows you to swap between the two, but if you’re looking for health, recovery, and sleep tracking and already own a regular watch, the Fitbit Air is the obvious choice.

It’s also worth noting here that, from a health perspective, you’re getting the same experience with the Fitbit Air, and it’s nearly half the price.

Fitbit promises seven days of battery life on both devices, and while I found that to be true with the Fitbit Air, no matter how many workouts I did, it was a different story with the Fitbit Edge.

It has been revealed that of course, this is largely down to the built-in GPS. Out of the box, the GPS on the device is automatically set to dynamic, which means it switches between using your phone’s GPS and the built-in GPS. When you switch the tracker to using the built-in GPS, I found it takes a hit on battery life, using around 11% for an hour-long run, and it didn’t last a full week.

  • "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It indicates a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Sources indicate that uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

Industry observers note that in order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any complications and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand upcoming arrival that the organization just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar concern recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations.
  • Sources indicate that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates.
  • If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with demonstrates you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Sources indicate that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of indicates and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

It has been revealed that if you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

According to recent reports, if you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized consumers may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

In a recent development, hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

Recent findings suggest that if you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your strategy. You can revision your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that have you noticed that there's these yellow cargo containers all over Leonida? Did you know that you can actually get inside of them to get rare weapons, explosives, vehicles, and so much more! It's yet another one of those hidden aspects of GTA 6 that you can't help but go out of your way to find more of, once you know to start looking.

Sources indicate that if you want to break into yellow Scoop containers in GTA 6, you're going to need to get a vital piece of equipment first: the Cut-Off Tool. Below I'm going to walk you through how to unlock the GTA 6 Cut-Off Tool and explain how it can be used to break into those Scoop containers.

Industry observers note that the Cut-Off Tool is one of the main pieces of GTA 6 equipment that you'll unlock as you play through the story. While you'll likely come across those yellow Scoop containers in your travels, you won't be able to open any of them until you've played a key GTA 6 mission in Chapter 3. Meet the Heders is the third mission of that chapter, and it'll send you down to a dockyard. Once you're these, you'll automatically be assigned the equipment and can use it freely outside of the mission.

You need to locate yellow Scoop shipping containers. These can be in the most unlikely of places – on random beaches, next to gang hideouts, in random parking lots – all across Leonida. Once you've located one, walk up to its front doors and press Triangle/Y. This will prompt Jason or Lucia to equip the Cut-Off Tool. You'll need to squeeze R2/RT and keep the power within the pink segment of the semi-circle for a short while until you cut through the lock. Once you do, the doors will swing open and you're welcome to whatever you find inside.

  • Industry observers note that I will probably be in the ground when Bethesda finally releases The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel—which is kind of liberating.
  • Tainted Grail is unabashedly created in the mould of The Elder Scrolls, in that it is a primarily first-person fantasy RPG where flexibility is its superpower.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that welcome to Dungeon Master, PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. Grab a seat in our badly-lit tavern and please ignore the goblin puke.

Industry observers note that I will probably be in the ground when Bethesda finally releases The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel—which is kind of liberating. I have hype immunity. But what's even more liberating is the fact that there's already an RPG that does everything I want from an Elder Scrolls game—2025's Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avelon.

Tainted Grail is unabashedly created in the mould of The Elder Scrolls, in that it is a primarily first-person fantasy RPG where flexibility is its superpower. You chart your own course and effectively construct your class, enhancing skills by using them as much as possible. But it is not merely the Elder Scrolls we have at home—it captures the very best that this kind of RPG can offer, and in some ways manages to outdo Bethesda.

Industry observers note that this is apparent right from the get-go. In classic Elder Scrolls form, Tainted Grail begins with you banged up in a facility that incarcerates and studies unfortunates afflicted with a magical plague, of which you are one. Follow the critical path and you will meet a new friend, get in some tough fights and then escape.

By the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.

But this island asylum is big. Really big. It's full of locked doors, hidden rooms, large spaces ripe for some big brawls, a subterranean area waiting to be delved into, oodles of lore—there are hours of rooting around to be done. So I ignored the critical path, had a big old wander, and by the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.

While Tainted Grail is full of bespoke quests sending you off into the open world on countless adventures, these are really just designed to get you out the door so you can stumble upon something cool—a new enemy that will utterly destroy you, a powerful weapon hidden in a crypt, an eccentric immortal being who wants to make a deal. The vibe is very TTRPG, which isn't surprising, given that it's based on one.

Industry observers note that and these adventures are actually dangerous. Deadly, even. The villains of Tainted Grail hit hard, and early on you will feel horrifyingly vulnerable. Basic bandits and skeletons can easily spell your doom. And if you stay out at night, you're screwed. Avelon is a miserable, cruel place, cursed and plagued, and you will struggle.

Developer Questline didn't simply up the lethality and call it a day, though. Tainted Grail, unlike The Elder Scrolls, actually has a quality combat system that falls firmly into the skill-based category. It's no Dark Souls, but it's more Dark Souls than Skyrim. So that increased level of challenge feels earned because of the tools you have available to you, and the range of combat styles you can develop.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that with all the options you have at your disposal—which has been further enhanced by DLC additions, letting you, for example, go through this Arthurian fantasy RPG as a kung-fu master—it can be hard to commit to a build. I've been spellblading it up, with my alchemical skills helping to shore up my weaknesses, but every time I encounter a new piece of gear I wonder what else I could create. But you do need to commit eventually. This isn't a game for a jack of all trades.

While Bethesda is more deft at crafting believable, reactive lands, Tainted Grail's world design also deserves its flowers. It's a smaller space, divided into three main areas, and while you can absolutely muck around for hundreds of hours, you can experience most of what it has to offer in 50. But what you'll experience in those 50 hours is so much more meticulously designed, with Questline getting so much out of each location.

It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions.

In a recent development, it's a looker, too. What it lacks in fidelity it more than makes up for in the art design department, and it's another place where Dark Souls rears its gorgeously hideous head. Tainted Grail finds beauty in the grim misery of its fantastical post-apocalyptic realm. It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions—the arboreal and the horrific, the grounded and alien. Avelon is delightfully strange, and that makes exploration all the more thrilling.

Recent findings suggest that as games grow ever larger and more bloated, my appreciation for richer, better-scoped worlds like Avalon only grows. And this does not indicate a dearth of ambition on Questline's part. Tainted Grail is a complex, elaborate game that will happily devour your days and keep showing you new things.

Clearly people want this—Tainted Grail has done very well for itself, garnering more than 20,000 user reviews on Steam, where its rating sits at Very Positive. It's a reassuring reminder that you do not need a gargantuan studio and big publisher money to make a quality RPG in the Elder Scrolls style.

Sources indicate that we don't know how many people are working on Sentinel right now, but we can expect the number to be large. Skyrim had around 100 people working on it, and with Starfield that jumped to more than 400. Tainted Grail was made by 50 people. That's quite the achievement.

So if you're craving a side-quest-heavy sandbox RPG with plenty of sword fights and spellflinging, Tainted Grail should absolutely be your next port of call. And the good news is that there's a demo. No excuses. Go play it.
